paths.description: Homepage and primary news-discovery entry point; tested at desktop, mobile, dark, reduced-motion, crawler, network, performance, privacy, accessibility and memory conditions.
News category listing, representing section/list templates and mobile stability.
Standard editorial article, representing the core reading journey, metadata and server-rendering.
Research/product-style article, sampled because it is a distinct content family and template.
Unknown URL to inspect HTTP/error recovery presentation.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt its palette to dark or increased-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture, the live CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme or forced-colors/prefers-contrast rules, and Lighthouse also found default-state contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and introduce preference-driven semantic surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(); verify controls under forced colors.

findings.summary: The site does not explicitly preserve UI visibility under increased-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The live stylesheet probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling, while Lighthouse found baseline color-contrast failures, increasing the risk that metadata and controls remain hard to perceive.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatments for essential controls and text, avoid suppressing system colors, and verify the full consent/navigation UI in high-contrast mode.

findings.summary: Page and state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no view-transition rules on this multi-page news site; route changes therefore use abrupt document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article and category navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Persistent page chrome does not expose scroll-state-aware behavior.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found fixed/sticky chrome but no scroll-state container queries or scroll-timeline behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress/shrinking-header treatment to orient readers on long pages.

findings.summary: Two simultaneous unsolicited overlays obscure the primary content on every sampled path.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-page consent wall plus a push-notification prompt layered over it before interaction; on mobile the notification panel covers the consent title and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not request notifications on load. Consolidate consent into one accessible, non-overlapping surface with equal accept/reject controls and defer nonessential prompts until a user asks.

findings.summary: Overlay experiences are not represented by native dialog/popover semantics.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM exposes consent headings but the semantic probe found 0 dialog, 0 popover and 0 details elements while six fixed/sticky elements were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a modal dialog for required consent decisions and a popover for transient prompts, with native focus management and light-dismiss where appropriate.

findings.summary: Advertising and prompt chrome dominates the first viewport.
findings.evidence: Across homepage, category, article and 404 screenshots, the actual content is dimmed and mostly hidden behind consent and notification UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve the first viewport for editorial purpose and content; remove the notification nag and reduce consent chrome to the minimum legally required.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target affordances are insufficient.
findings.evidence: A focused primary anchor computed to outline-style none with no box shadow; Lighthouse failed target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible ring and increase control target boxes/spacing to at least the recommended touch size.

findings.summary: The primary reading journey is blocked before users can understand or use the page.
findings.evidence: All first-load screenshots foreground consent and push prompts rather than the page purpose, headline or next reading action.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the article/listing purpose and primary reading action visible immediately; defer notification acquisition and make consent non-obscuring where legally possible.

findings.summary: System and error states are obscured by unrelated prompts.
findings.evidence: The 404 page contains recovery content, but the screenshot shows it dimmed beneath the same two overlays, preventing immediate recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Suppress marketing/notification prompts on error pages and keep recovery links immediately operable.

findings.summary: Load performance misses the Core Web Vitals bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 14.1 s, CLS 0.172 and performance 0.55; the first-party trace measured LCP 4.04 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the real LCP resource, remove early third-party competition, and reserve late content space.

findings.summary: Category and article templates shift visibly after load.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout captures measured CLS 0.203 on the category page and 0.117 on the article; Lighthouse measured 0.172 on home.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve ad/banner slots, stabilize font metrics and prevent late prompt/content insertion from moving the page.

findings.summary: Critical resource delivery is dominated by third-party and render-blocking work.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 94 requests and 2.11 MB, including 1.95 MB third-party bytes; Lighthouse estimated 950 ms render-blocking savings and 610 KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay ad/analytics code until consent and idle/interaction, remove parser-blocking scripts, and improve cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Substantial unused JavaScript and CSS are shipped on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 429 KiB unused JavaScript and 35 KiB unused CSS; 32 scripts transferred 1.58 MB in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split page features and conditionally load advertising, analytics and consent integrations only when needed.

findings.summary: Images and controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 97 of 100 images without alt; Lighthouse failed image-alt, button-name and link-name.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful editorial images descriptive alt, mark decorative images empty-alt, and add accessible names to icon buttons/links.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit failed on the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust semantic color tokens to WCAG contrast thresholds and test all prompt, metadata and navigation text.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is not coherent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the DOM probe found no main landmark and a heading sequence beginning H3, H2 with multiple consent H1s injected alongside page headings.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one content H1 per page, sequential section headings, a main landmark and properly contained consent-dialog headings.

findings.summary: Viewport scaling policy and small targets impair zoom/reflow use.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because maximum-scale is 1 and failed target-size, although 360px layouts did avoid horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale=1, retain user-scalable=yes, and enlarge closely spaced controls.

findings.summary: The page triggers notification permission on startup and logs browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed notification-on-start and inspector-issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notification permission only after an explicit user gesture and resolve Chrome Issues-panel warnings.

findings.summary: Transport and cookie defenses are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and nosniff are present, but headers evidence found no CSP or HSTS; cookie evidence found 10 cookies flagged insecure, including several without Secure and many SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforced CSP and HSTS, set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is essential.

findings.summary: Third-party tracking is disproportionate to the first-load reading task.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 27 third-party origins and seven known trackers; HAR attributed 75 of 94 requests and 1.95 of 2.11 MB to third parties before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Block nonessential tracking until informed consent, reduce vendors, batch analytics and document the minimum data required.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested out of context on load.
findings.evidence: The initial screenshot shows a notification-acquisition overlay before user intent, and Lighthouse failed notification-on-start.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notifications only after a user chooses a clearly labelled subscribe action and understands the value.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no HSTS, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or CSP; X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a restrictive Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and CSP frame-ancestors/script controls.

findings.summary: Overlay composition is not resilient at narrow viewports.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the notification panel overlaps and clips the consent experience, hiding its title and upper controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure only one top-layer interaction is open, constrain it to the viewport and test nested third-party UI at narrow sizes.

findings.summary: Consent presents acceptance prominently without an equally direct reject choice and is paired with notification nagging.
findings.evidence: Initial screenshots show primary Consent and Manage options buttons but no visible Reject all action, while a second unsolicited notification panel competes above it.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer equally prominent accept and reject actions, remove the simultaneous notification nag, and make later withdrawal easy.

findings.summary: Editorial image delivery is not consistently modern or responsive.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 37 legacy-format images, no detected modern-format images and one oversized image; the sampled elements generally lacked srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants with srcset/sizes and right-size each editorial thumbnail and hero.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume most transferred bytes for a text/news landing page.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 1.95 MB third-party transfer out of 2.11 MB total; ad code alone included a 642 KiB script and trackers reported 27 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer advertising and analytics, and remove vendors that do not produce measurable reader value.

taskList.title: Remove the startup notification prompt and redesign consent as one accessible, equal-choice surface
Gate and reduce third-party advertising/analytics to recover privacy, LCP and page weight
Repair accessible names, heading/landmark structure, focus, targets and zoom
Add CSP/HSTS and tighten cookie/referrer/permissions policies
Stabilize ad/banner/font slots across listing and article templates
Modernize responsive image delivery and user-preference theming
Add progressive navigation polish and resolve inspector issues
